title: Orchestration as its own plugin
summary: Stage 2 of the plugin split, after the prose gate: builds the steward-orchestration plugin, whose session-start hook creates the session registry and tells the model to check its role, and moves the orchestrating skill into it. The old steward plugin keeps running unchanged beside it.
motivation: Steward 0.14.2 is one 1,638-line hook script doing four jobs for four harnesses, so a user cannot take one part, one switch turns off two gates, and personal text ships to everyone (docs/roadmap/plugin-split.md, Why).

included: Shape: a set of three binders, because the operator asked for small separate binders (test 1): steward-prose-gate, then this one (after: steward-prose-gate), then steward-delegation (after: steward-orchestration). Each validates and leaves the suite green on its own.

Design steps 7 and 8 of docs/roadmap/plugin-split.md 'Build sequence', which is the source of truth for every file, contract and done-check: the orchestration hook (7) and the orchestration content and packaging (8). One item per step.

Branch: hatch builds from plugin-split (local git config hatch.defaultBranch=plugin-split). The operator merges the steward-prose-gate integration branch into plugin-split before this binder's delivery starts, so everything its contracts create exists at this binder's base: plugins/steward-prose-gate/**, its scripts.test segment, its entries in both root catalogs, and its pi extension. The operator merges this binder's integration branch into plugin-split before steward-delegation starts.

New plugin folder plugins/steward-orchestration/. Outside it this binder edits only package.json (scripts.test gains the plugin's unittest run), .claude-plugin/marketplace.json (one entry; orchestration is Claude Code only, so the Codex catalog gets none), tests/test_catalogs.py (every non-pinned entry resolves to its plugin manifest) and tests/test_no_opus_max.py (the template path), and git-moves skills/orchestrating/ into the plugin.

The monolith keeps working as it is: hooks/steward_hook.py still creates the registry, skills/delegating/SKILL.md keeps its Role check, and tests/test_steward_hook.py keeps its registry tests until steward-delegation retires them. Two hooks creating the registry is harmless: each writes only when the file is missing.

Item check for every item: `PI_SUBAGENTS_DIR=/nonexistent npm test` from the repo root, expect 'fail 0'. npm test runs package.json scripts.test; at this binder's base it is `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests && python3 -m unittest discover -s plugins/steward-prose-gate/tests && node --test 'tests/pi/*.test.mjs' 'plugins/*/tests/pi/*.test.mjs'`. node stays the last segment joined by &&, so its 'fail 0' line prints only when every unittest run before it passed.

Reference totals measured at 2e351f8 on this machine, 2026-10-24, with PI_SUBAGENTS_DIR=/nonexistent: root Python 'Ran 610 tests', 'OK (skipped=13)'; node 'tests 102', 'pass 102', 'fail 0'. steward-prose-gate adds its own unittest run and node cases before this binder starts, so the first item measures the real base totals.

Totals rule: every item's commit message body lists the suite totals at its base and after it (each unittest 'Ran N tests' line and the node 'tests N' line). Totals change only by tests the item adds, moves or names as retired.

Known machine mismatch, not caused by the split: PI_SUBAGENTS_DIR=/nonexistent skips the 13 tests that need an installed pi-subagents. Two of them fail at c5fd21b on this machine when not skipped, because pi-subagents 0.82.0 is installed and 0.78.0 is mirrored: tests/test_pi_model_plan_apply.py:575 (test_version_is_pinned) and tests/test_pi_model_plan_resolver.py:27 (the mirrored constant; the failing assertion, test_installed_version_is_the_mirrored_one, is at :260).
File-level done-checks from the design are oracle assertions. Scratch-session checks (`claude --plugin-dir ...`) are not; they belong to manual step 21.
Repo rules for every item: one commit per item; never rebase; no agent attribution in commit messages; no em-dashes in shipped texts; Markdown tables use the |-|-| separator.

Runtime: Node 22.18 or newer runs the TypeScript pi extensions without a build step (README.md, 'Pi' section); hook scripts are stdlib Python 3.9 or newer (hooks/steward_hook.py:5). No file pins either.
Env: the repo has no environment to start; tests run directly. env_contract.command only reports the two runtimes.
excluded: Manual steps already done (design 'Build sequence', Status note): step 0, the tag v0.14.2 exists at f13555b; step 1, both root catalogs pin steward to v0.14.2, with the README notice and tests/test_catalogs.py.

Later binder steward-delegation: design steps 9-12, 14 and 16-20, including the Role check leaving the delegation edict (16), the monolith and its registry code being deleted (18), and the root README rewrite that drops the sauron quote at README.md:447 (20).

After the binders, manual step 21: live checks on Claude Code, Copilot, Codex and pi; the full suite without PI_SUBAGENTS_DIR, including the 13 pi-subagents tests; and the scratch-session checks of steps 6, 14 and 17, plus a `claude --plugin-dir plugins/steward-orchestration` session that shows the registry and the role-check block.
Manual step 22: merge plugin-split to main with --no-ff and create the per-plugin tags (steward-orchestration--v0.15.0 and the others); the operator authorizes the push.
Manual step 23: the operator's machine checklist, including writing ~/.claude/orchestration/edict.md from `git show v0.14.2:skills/orchestrating/SKILL.md` line 21.
Manual step 24: plainlanguage manifests in the common-skills repo.
Edits to the operator's personal files (~/AGENTS.md, ~/.claude/orchestration/edict.md, prose-patterns files).
Orchestration on pi, Copilot or Codex (operator decided: Claude Code only), and the follow-ups carried from orchestration-split.md (the memory rule, session identity by name, stale registry rows).
Design non-goals relevant here: harness dependency fields; migration code that reads old config paths; cross-plugin imports.

design_facts.stack: Agent-harness plugins for Claude Code, Copilot CLI, Codex CLI and pi: stdlib Python 3.9+ hook scripts, TypeScript pi extensions run by Node 22.18+ type stripping, JSON manifests and Markdown skills; tests are Python unittest and node:test; no third-party dependencies.

work_items.title: Orchestration hook that sets up the registry
work_items.summary: Add the orchestration plugin's session-start hook, which creates the session registry once and tells the model to check its role, with its tests.

contract.design: docs/roadmap/plugin-split.md: Build sequence step 7; steward-orchestration (its SessionStart hook does two things); Hook split (Hook entries, orchestration row; Map of hooks/steward_hook.py, O rows 73-79, 91-104, 111-124, 140-147); Config, state and env vars (registry row); Tests (SessionStartTests row).
does: Create plugins/steward-orchestration/hooks/orchestration_hook.py: stdlib Python 3.9+, called as `orchestration_hook.py <harness> <mode>`. Only `claude session-start` does anything. An unknown harness or mode exits 0 with no output, and any exception exits 0 (fail open).

Copy from hooks/steward_hook.py per the map's O rows: get_orchestration_dir (73-79: env STEWARD_ORCHESTRATION_DIR, else ~/.claude/orchestration under HOME, deliberately not $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, so config profiles share one registry), _non_empty_str (103-104) only if used, REGISTRY_SKELETON (111-124) with the skill named `steward-orchestration:orchestrating` (today `steward:orchestrating` at :117) and its separator row written |-|-|-|-|-|, _ensure_registry (140-147), and its own _dispatch and main.

claude session-start, step 1: create <orchestration dir>/initiatives.md from the skeleton when it is missing and never overwrite it. Best effort: an OSError is swallowed and step 2 still runs, as hooks/steward_hook.py:449-454 does today.

Step 2: print {"hookSpecificOutput": {"hookEventName": "SessionStart", "additionalContext": <block>}}. The block holds the Role check paragraph moved from skills/delegating/SKILL.md:41-42, with the skill named `steward-orchestration:orchestrating`, and this sentence verbatim: 'This plugin relies on steward-delegation. If the `steward-delegation:delegating` skill is not in your skill list, tell the operator once.'

Create plugins/steward-orchestration/hooks/hooks.json for Claude Code: one SessionStart entry, matcher startup|resume|clear|compact|fork, timeout 10, command `python3 "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/orchestration_hook.py" claude session-start`.

No import of, and no path into, another plugin folder or hooks/steward_hook.py. No file under plugins/steward-orchestration names steward_hook, carries a `steward:` namespace, or carries em-dash text.
package.json scripts.test gains ` && python3 -m unittest discover -s plugins/steward-orchestration/tests` before the node segment; node stays the last segment, joined by &&.
tests: plugins/steward-orchestration/tests/test_orchestration_hook.py, with its own small temp-dir base case (no shared helpers module), ports test_registry_created_once, test_registry_not_overwritten and test_unwritable_orchestration_dir_still_emits_context (tests/test_steward_hook.py:166-210) to `orchestration_hook.py claude session-start`, and adds: the block carries the Role check and the relies-on sentence; the created registry names steward-orchestration:orchestrating and uses the |-|-| separator; an unknown harness and an unknown mode exit 0 with no output; a hooks.json case (one SessionStart entry, matcher, timeout 10, command naming orchestration_hook.py with the claude argument).
The originals stay in tests/test_steward_hook.py; this binder does not touch them.
contract.red_when: The registry is missing after a first run or overwritten on a second; an unwritable orchestration dir loses the block; the block lacks the relies-on sentence or names steward:orchestrating; the discover segment is missing from scripts.test (the run then prints no plugins/steward-orchestration unittest line, which the totals assertion catches).
contract.repo_rules: One commit for this item; never rebase; no agent attribution in the commit message; no em-dash in shipped text; Markdown tables use the |-|-| separator.

signals: contract:new-surface: orchestration_hook.py <harness> <mode> CLI and a Claude Code SessionStart hook in a new plugin

contract:existing-surface: the registry ~/.claude/orchestration/initiatives.md and env STEWARD_ORCHESTRATION_DIR keep their names; the skeleton written for a new registry names steward-orchestration:orchestrating (an existing registry is never rewritten)
blast-radius: package.json scripts.test is also edited by items in the other two binders of the set
not-computed:sensitive-zone (no per-repo sensitive-path setting and no .hatch config to match against)

assertions: `PI_SUBAGENTS_DIR=/nonexistent npm test` exits 0 from the repo root: every unittest run ends with an OK line (skips only the 13 pi-subagents tests), node ends with fail 0, and the printed totals change only by tests this item adds, moves or names as retired.
The run prints one more unittest result than at the item's base (plugins/steward-orchestration/tests); the root and plugins/steward-prose-gate totals are unchanged.

test_orchestration_hook.py holds the three ported registry cases, a block-content case (Role check plus the relies-on sentence), unknown harness and unknown mode cases, and a hooks.json case with timeout 10.
`grep -rn steward_hook plugins/steward-orchestration` prints nothing (positive control: the same grep on hooks/hooks.json prints its five command lines).
`grep -rnE 'steward:[a-z]' plugins/steward-orchestration` prints nothing (positive control: the same grep on hooks/steward_hook.py hits line 117, the old REGISTRY_SKELETON).

work_items.title: Move the orchestrating skill into its plugin and package it
work_items.summary: Move the orchestrating skill and onboarding template into the orchestration plugin, take the operator's personal edict and the em-dash rule out of them, and give the plugin its manifest, README and catalog entry.

contract.design: Build sequence step 8; steward-orchestration; Names (orchestrating rows); Personal content ('sauron' edict; Em-dash rule, onboarding-template.md:13); Versions and tags; Repo layout after the reorg (catalog entries); Dependencies: manual on every harness (steward-orchestration row); Release and migration (orchestration README); Tests (new root test_catalogs.py).
does: `git mv skills/orchestrating plugins/steward-orchestration/skills/orchestrating` (SKILL.md and onboarding-template.md), so history is kept as renames.

Names in both files: `steward:delegating` becomes `steward-delegation:delegating`, `steward:orchestrating` becomes `steward-orchestration:orchestrating`, and the seven `steward:<profile>` names in template item 3 (onboarding-template.md:11) become `steward-delegation:<profile>`.

Personal content out: remove the operator's quoted 'sauron' edict (SKILL.md:21, onboarding-template.md:15). In its place the skill says: if `<registry dir>/edict.md` exists (~/.claude/orchestration/edict.md, or the same name under $STEWARD_ORCHESTRATION_DIR), the primary sends its text verbatim in the onboarding message and secondaries follow it. The template gets the matching instruction. No code reads edict.md.

Em-dash text out: drop 'no em-dashes in prose for the operator' from template item 5 (onboarding-template.md:13). Keep the sentence 'Claude Opus never runs at max' in the template; tests/test_no_opus_max.py checks it.

Create plugins/steward-orchestration/.claude-plugin/plugin.json: name steward-orchestration, "version": "0.15.0", description, author, repository, license; no dependencies field; skills and hooks at their default paths (skills/, hooks/hooks.json). No Codex or Copilot manifest (Claude Code only).

Create plugins/steward-orchestration/README.md: what the plugin does (primary and secondary roles, Claude Code only); that it relies on steward-delegation, installed by hand (no dependency field); install with `claude plugin install steward-orchestration@steward`; the registry path and STEWARD_ORCHESTRATION_DIR; the optional operator-owned edict.md; that Copilot lists it from the shared catalog but it is Claude Code only. No sauron text.

.claude-plugin/marketplace.json gains {name: steward-orchestration, description, source: ./plugins/steward-orchestration}. .agents/plugins/marketplace.json is not changed. The pinned steward entries stay untouched.

tests/test_catalogs.py gains one case per catalog: every entry other than the pinned steward resolves to an existing plugin folder whose manifest carries the entry's name (Claude catalog: <folder>/.claude-plugin/plugin.json; Codex catalog: <folder>/.codex-plugin/plugin.json, local source path). This also covers the steward-prose-gate entries already present.
tests/test_no_opus_max.py: the template path in EDICTS (:19) points at plugins/steward-orchestration/skills/orchestrating/onboarding-template.md.
tests: plugins/steward-orchestration/tests/test_orchestration_content.py: manifest name steward-orchestration, version 0.15.0, no dependencies field; skill frontmatter name orchestrating; no 'sauron' and no `steward:` names in the skill or the template; both name edict.md; the template keeps 'Claude Opus never runs at max'.
contract.notes: The root README still quotes the sauron edict (README.md:447) until steward-delegation's docs item rewrites it. After the move the in-tree root plugin no longer ships the orchestrating skill; nobody installs the root, since both catalogs pin v0.14.2.
contract.red_when: A non-pinned catalog entry does not resolve to its manifest (test_catalogs fails); the template loses the no-Opus-max rule; sauron text, an em-dash rule or a steward: name survives in the plugin; skills/orchestrating still exists at the root.
contract.repo_rules: One commit for this item; never rebase; no agent attribution in the commit message; no em-dash in shipped text; Markdown tables use the |-|-| separator.

signals: contract:existing-surface: the skill name steward:orchestrating becomes steward-orchestration:orchestrating; the Claude catalog gains an entry (additive)
destructive: the operator's quoted edict leaves shipped text; it moves to an operator-owned edict.md that this binder does not write (manual step 23)
blast-radius: tests/test_no_opus_max.py and tests/test_catalogs.py are also edited by steward-delegation items
not-computed:sensitive-zone (no per-repo sensitive-path setting and no .hatch config to match against)

assertions: `PI_SUBAGENTS_DIR=/nonexistent npm test` exits 0 from the repo root: every unittest run ends with an OK line (skips only the 13 pi-subagents tests), node ends with fail 0, and the printed totals change only by tests this item adds, moves or names as retired.

plugins/steward-orchestration/skills/orchestrating/ holds SKILL.md and onboarding-template.md, and `git ls-files skills/orchestrating` prints nothing. (No rename-detection check: the edits to the short template can drop git's similarity score below its rename threshold.)
`grep -rn sauron plugins/` prints nothing (positive control: `git show HEAD~1:skills/orchestrating/SKILL.md | grep -c sauron` prints 1).
`grep -rnE 'steward:[a-z]' plugins/steward-orchestration` prints nothing (positive control: `git show HEAD~1:skills/orchestrating/onboarding-template.md | grep -cE 'steward:[a-z]'` prints 3).
`grep -rniE 'em.?dash|EM_DASH|u2014' plugins/steward-orchestration` prints nothing (positive control: the same pattern on `git show HEAD~1:skills/orchestrating/onboarding-template.md` hits line 13).
`grep -c 'Claude Opus never runs at max' plugins/steward-orchestration/skills/orchestrating/onboarding-template.md` prints 1 or more, and tests/test_no_opus_max.py reads the template from that path.

plugins/steward-orchestration/.claude-plugin/plugin.json has name steward-orchestration, "version": "0.15.0" and no dependencies field; .claude-plugin/marketplace.json has a steward-orchestration entry with source ./plugins/steward-orchestration; .agents/plugins/marketplace.json has no steward-orchestration entry.
tests/test_catalogs.py passes with its new per-catalog resolve cases, and the steward entries still pin v0.14.2.
